description:
[FILED BY: Polybius the Grand (user-tier) — PRINCIPAL-directed roadmap item 2026-07-05. PROBLEM FRAMING — the team owns the fix shape. DO NOT PICK UP until the secure-core Phase-1 arc (stoa--po5) lands; that arc is also the measurement baseline for this question.]

PROBLEM: the gauntlet's decomposition granularity (small envelopes, many dispatches, verification seats between micro-steps) was tuned for Opus-4.7-era floor models. Field evidence reviewed by the Grand + PRINCIPAL (practitioner workflow transcript, 2026-07-05): current-generation models carry design->build->test END-TO-END over multi-hour runs — one session, ~12 merged PRs, gated only by automated reviewers, with a heavier post-hoc verification pass finding nothing to fix. If our floor models can carry bigger envelopes, then our cost-per-shipped-change is dominated by DISPATCH OVERHEAD + seat-to-seat context loss, not by build quality.

DESIGN QUESTION for the team: re-tier WHAT the gauntlet gates. Candidate shape (not prescriptive): fewer, bigger envelopes where the executor carries design->build->test end-to-end; the independent seats (plan-critic, verifier, reviewer, ground-truth auditor) reposition as gates at OUTCOME checkpoints rather than between micro-steps. The seats' value concentrates where it is strongest: independence, falsification, ground-truth audit, bw institutional memory.

NOT in question (load-bearing, keep): seat independence properties (e.g. the plan-critic never proposes fixes; the verifier falsifies), seat identity/accountability in commits + bw, and the >=2-independent-checkers-per-artifact discipline. What MAY change: checkpoint placement + envelope size + the INTERIOR mechanism of seats (a reviewer seat may fan out dynamic, task-chosen reviewer lenses via a composed workflow instead of any fixed interior roster — seats = governance, workflows = mechanism).

INPUT DATA: the envelope-telemetry discipline (plan with the Grand, ticket to follow) records wall-clock + files-touched + expected-vs-actual size at every close; stoa--po5's arc provides the fresh overhead datapoint. Bring that data to this design.

SEQUENCING: engage after stoa--po5 lands. Pairs with the goal-mode-floor roadmap ticket (sibling, filed same day — id in first comment).
